implementation.removed: Infallible DMA frame clone beneath MEMORY_OBJECTS after shared/exclusive counters were incremented.
implementation.preparation: Copy and DMA share inert vector capacity preparation outside memory serialization with no source pin, frame borrow or copied frame identity. Existing typed admission and completion owners stay separate.
implementation.publication: DMA rechecks captured full namespace generation, object ID, size, direction/read-write rights, loan/retirement/copy/DMA exclusions, CPU mappings and checked counters. Snapshot fill and both counters publish under one memory hold without allocation.
implementation.failure: Ordinary unused/rejected capacity explicitly disposes post-memory guard. Vector allocation rejection returns FrameAllocFailed; backend conversions remain Error::Memory. No descriptor/domain/engine claim precedes this pin factory.
implementation.lifetime: Bare DmaPin fallback retains snapshot, shared/exclusive counters and original backing without allocator/registry entry. Explicit unpin frees snapshot before original counter decrement, then deferred backing release after registry unlock. Missing object is a pinned-object invariant rejection, matching copy; absence is no hardware proof.
implementation.containing_owners: VT-d, AMD-Vi and SMMU map entries retain existing DmaOperation exact root/public capability. Original PendingPin and MappingMaintenance own completed pins and typed hardware obligations through unit readiness/maintenance/rollback/quarantine.
remaining: independent snapshot byte/count and aggregate principal admission for overlapping/retained vectors
source-transfer/scoped cleanup, other ordinary backing rollback and broader caller/destructor/IRQ contexts
concurrent hardware I/O, sustained pressure, essential-service latency and full recovery matrix

selected_dma_guarded_retention.qualification: Memory-only pin never handed to IOMMU; unpin controls use unused pins, not synthetic hardware completion.
